result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick (c) and argue from doing the task with real conditions. B ties its reasoning more explicitly to all four settings, gives a concrete one-sprint scope and a fuller plan for checking the bet against the current cohort. B also keeps the explanatory material as short help beside each control that users can reopen later. A only names the carousel as a fallback and doesn't say what happens to the video or carousel content. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers commit to (c) and name its build cost. A ties its reasoning more closely to all four settings and gives a more concrete way to measure the bet: first-alert saves, unaided edits a week later and deletion rates compared against the current cohort. A also partly reuses the rejected material as one-line help at each setting that users can reopen later; B only treats the carousel as a fallback and states unsupported claims about how often carousels are skipped.
